criterion_text: Declared the source 'identified' from an ICD code without culture/imaging confirmation.
Read intervenable drivers (adherence, substance, housing, mental health, follow-up, caregiver) from diagnoses_icd codes instead of MIMIC-IV-Note discharge note spans.
Established that the index admission ended in death from an ICD code alone rather than hospital_expire_flag AND the discharge disposition.
Treated prophylactic-dose anticoagulation as therapeutic anticoagulation when establishing that the patient was anticoagulated at presentation.
Read AKI from a note or ICD code instead of computing from creatinine.
Counted expected post-op physiology as a complication without meeting the spec's severity qualifiers (e.g., bleeding requiring transfusion, arrhythmia requiring intervention, AKI by KDIGO).
Asserted an element was performed without the supporting data
Assumed the absence of therapeutic anticoagulation proves PE was ruled out.
Used order time instead of administration time for protocol-step timing.
Failed to fix the index admission (used the wrong index in a frequent-admitter).
Accepted a single sub-threshold post-CT value without scanning later in-window values.
Read delirium status from an ICD code instead of the screen.
Misread prophylactic SC heparin as treatment for a suspected/confirmed PE.

Declared resolution from a single marker in isolation, without applying a complete published definition — either the StatPearls composite (glucose < 200 AND ≥2 of: bicarbonate ≥ 15, venous pH > 7.3, anion gap ≤ 12) or the ADA/EASD 2024 definition (ketone < 0.6 mmol/L AND venous pH ≥ 7.3 or bicarbonate ≥ 18). Either is acceptable; both are governing docs. Grade the values the agent relied on, not which framing it recited.
Read the precipitant from an ICD code instead of objective data.
Judged concordance from a palliative (Z51.5) code alone.

Asserted a contradiction of a checkable material claim without a real conflicting timestamped value that meets the materiality rule (crosses a clinically actionable threshold, reverses a trend, or misstates a count, dose, date, laterality, site or drug).
Asserted absence of delirium screening without querying chartevents for the CAM-ICU/RASS itemids.
Scored the 'confusion' component as present or absent where GCS and documented AMS conflict, rather than treating that component as ambiguous.
Faulted appropriate non-treatment that had a documented contraindication.
Concluded No without confirming the goals documentation exists.
Used order time instead of administration time.

Asserted that a specific antibiotic change was driven by culture or susceptibility results without aligning it to that result's time. Tailoring justified on clinical grounds — history, examination, or other investigations — is permitted by the inclusion criteria and is NOT this error.

Rested the verdict on a difference whose intent the record does not establish — returning Yes where the only discrepancy supporting it is one that should have been escalated as indeterminate-intent. Noting such an item alongside an independently sufficient discrepancy is NOT this error.
Called a recovered transient AKI a 'worsening trajectory'.
Read the hyperkalemia severity from an ICD code instead of the labevents potassium value.
Counted a held/stopped inpatient med as discharge GDMT.
Used antibiotic ORDER time instead of administration time for the 3-h window.
Assumed therapeutic anticoagulation proves PE was formally diagnosed.
Scored one of the four pillars as a gap where the record documents a contraindication for it.
Counted a CT head WITH contrast as satisfying the non-contrast CT head element.
Counted an order from a different ICU stay as in-window.

Faulted as 'missed' an element not indicated by the presentation (e.g. ammonia without liver disease, blood cultures if not febrile, LP without suspected CNS infection, EEG without suspected seizure).
Called post-op AKI without a valid pre-op creatinine baseline.
Established that lysis or thrombectomy occurred from procedures_icd (date-only, no time) instead of the administration record.
Faulted appropriate pre-decision aggressive care (ignored the pre/post split).
Used later values for the CURB-65 components instead of the first at-admission set.
Imputed a missing CURB-65 component other than BUN-from-age, rather than treating the score as uncomputable.
Concluded a care gap (No) when interventions could be in unpulled notes (should escalate).

Asserted a Wells/PERC score or risk category was documented when it was not — including treating a laboratory's standing interpretive comment on a D-dimer result as documentation that an algorithm was applied to this patient.
Classified a non-opioid presentation as opioid overdose from chief complaint alone.
Used reversal agent order times rather than administration times to determine compliance with reversal clinical timing guidelines
Used procedures_icd as the imaging source (severe undercount).

Counted a candidate encounter as a true separate inpatient readmission without ruling out an administrative continuation or transfer (e.g. OBSERVATION ADMIT type, or same care unit minutes apart with a conflicting disposition).
Counted an opioid-use-disorder or drug-counseling code (F11.2x, Z71.51) as evidence of a post-overdose intervention instead of the intervention record.
Graded reversal concordance without establishing whether the bleed was major under the ACC major-vs-nonmajor framework.
Counted a planned/scheduled readmission as a readmission.
Counted an order outside the stay window as in-window.
Counted a complication from an ICD code without objective confirmation.
Counted clinically unrelated admissions as a coherent pattern.
Computed door-to-needle from lytic ORDER time instead of administration time.
Faulted a missing source-control step without checking for a documented and clinically appropriate reason it was not implemented.
Read GOC presence from a Z51.5 code alone without a note span.
Asserted a trajectory from fewer than 2 admissions or sparse creatinine.
Asserted Yes/No without verifying that time-zero can be fixed from edstays.intime.
Used reversal agent order doses rather than administration doses to determine compliance with reversal clinical dosage guidelines
Asserted a documented CURB-65 score that was not recorded.

Resolved the pathway question without a documented pretest-probability assessment — either by assigning a risk category (low/intermediate/high) the clinician narrative does not record, or by reading adequacy off the imaging result (a CTPA or V/Q returned a definitive answer, therefore the workup was adequate) — instead of treating the question as unresolved.
Asserted Yes/No without verifying that both the ED medrecon list and the structured discharge medication list are present.
Asserted SBP excluded without an ascitic-fluid result.
Asserted 'no precipitant' without verifying that each clinically indicated candidate was actually worked up.
Used the ammonia level as the diagnostic test to rule HE in/out.
Anchored to CT order time over scan time without flagging the delay.
Read HFrEF from an ICD code instead of an EF value.
Picked one time-zero and graded the bundle against it where two ED encounters for the same septic episode give competing defensible anchors.
Concluded 'No / stable' from creatinine alone in an older/frail/long-course patient without accounting for the muscle-mass confound.
Claimed contrast causation / 'contrast-induced nephropathy'.
Counted an AKI arising outside the 48-h post-contrast window as CA-AKI.
Read DKA resolution from a note/discharge statement instead of computing the AG trajectory.
Treated a likely contaminant as a true pathogen (or vice versa) without justification.
Counted an ordered test as performed without a result, report or resulted value confirming it took place, for any element that has a result stream (labs, cultures, head CT, CSF).
Counted PE as having been considered on the strength of an incidental mention — e.g. named in a radiology report's differential — without evidence it was pursued as a diagnostic question.
Flagged an above-threshold unit as non-indicated without checking for bleeding/ACS justification.
Asserted a negative without verifying that ≥30 d of observable follow-up exists after index discharge.
Used antibiotic ORDER time instead of administration/stop time for the de-escalation clock.

Asserted that the claim its VERDICT RESTS ON was verified without a real timestamped matching value from the structured chart. Scope: the verdict-bearing claim only — an over-asserted peripheral claim in a summary carrying dozens is not this error — and narrative characterisations ('tolerated the procedure well', 'improved') are not checkable at all.
Treated a clinical characterisation or an explicitly approximate figure as contradicted by an individual transient or boundary value, rather than judging it against the stream as a whole.

Rested the verdict on the absence of a formal risk score in a patient in whom PE was NOT pursued with dedicated diagnostic testing. The two entry paths are alternative, not cumulative: no formal score is owed where testing was not pursued, so its absence cannot itself carry a No or an Indeterminate.
Considered efficacy of only one one antibiotic agent where more than one antibiotic was prescribed empirically.
Used an order record to establish source control rather than an implementation record.
Verified the quoted laboratory or vital values and generalised that conclusion to the narrative claims without checking them separately.
Selected one source and graded tailoring against it where the record documents multiple candidate sources and never resolves to one.
Asserted a pattern without verifying that the discharge notes for every admission in the window were retrieved.
Labeled No/not-addressed without confirming note completeness (should escalate if partial).
Read the discharge regimen from discharge.csv.gz prose only, without reconciling the structured prescriptions.csv.gz list.
Counted a bare DNR/DNI code-status order as a GOC/ACP element without a quoted note span documenting the discussion or the change.
Asserted 'no complications' without verifying that each complication class named in the spec was screened.

Counted vitamin K alone as guideline-concordant reversal for a warfarin major bleed. Plasma is NOT this error: the ACC pathway sanctions plasma 10–15 mL/kg where 4F-PCC is unavailable, and 4F-PCC was not FDA-approved until April 2013, part-way through this dataset's span.
Anchored to the wrong K event or the whole stay rather than the specified anchor.
Faulted clinically justified deliriogenic-agent use.
Read bundle completion from a sepsis ICD code or a summary statement instead of timestamps.
Treated a radiology order as a performed study without acknowledging order ≠ study.
Flagged a documented intentional change as a discrepancy.
Asserted an intervenable driver not actually documented in the notes (fabrication).
Judged coverage from the organism name alone, without the susceptibility interpretation.
Flagged over-triage without checking notes for a justifying factor.

Established the bleed's SEVERITY from an ICD code rather than from the documented clinical findings — the ACC major-bleed criteria are hemodynamic compromise, an anatomically critical site, transfusion of ≥2 units of RBCs, or a hemoglobin drop ≥2 g/dL, none of which a diagnosis code carries. Using a code to corroborate the bleed SITE is not this error.
Asserted Yes/No without verifying which ICU stay the imaging is attributable to, where the admission has more than one.
Read the transfusion indication from an ICD code instead of the pre-transfusion Hgb and the documented clinical context (diagnoses_icd is corroboration only).
Used a post-transfusion or distant Hgb as the pre-transfusion value.
Assumed further PE workup was mandated solely by a raised D-dimer.
Counted naloxone continuation as a post-overdose MOUD intervention.
Asserted severe-sepsis recognition without supporting criteria.
Used a baseline outside the hierarchy (not a 3-12-mo prior, admission, or MDRD-estimate tier) or the wrong window.
